clue.text: Too easy as the Italian gets mug running round

indicators.note: running round says the slang word for a mug is wrapped about the Italian article

parts.note: mug is slang for the face
il is the Italian for 'the'

explanation.surface: An Italian man finds something too easy as he jogs around holding a mug.
explanation.definitionFit: Facile describes something achieved with too little effort, glib or oversimplified, so too easy fits well.

clue.text: Finished puzzled? That's typical of the Toughie!

indicators.note: puzzled suggests confusion, so the letters of the preceding word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A solver who has just finished a puzzle exclaims that it was typical of the Telegraph's hard Toughie series.
explanation.walkthrough: The Toughie is the Telegraph's harder daily crossword, so a fiendish difficulty is just what you would expect of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiendish means extremely difficult, the hallmark of the paper's tougher puzzle series.

clue.text: Reduction in staff resulting in shortage at the top?

definitions.meaning: a cut in the number of crew members working a ship or plane
a very short haircut leaves little hair on the head

explanation.surface: Layoffs leave a company without enough senior managers.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is a cut to the crew; the second turns 'the top' from senior management into the top of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a staff cutback, and a close-cropped hairstyle leaving scant hair on top.

clue.text: Toad's disguise from Los Angeles strip

parts.note: to strip is to take one's clothes off

explanation.surface: A disguise worn on a Los Angeles street, the Strip.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Wind in the Willows, Mr Toad escapes from prison dressed as a washerwoman.
explanation.definitionFit: Toad of Toad Hall escapes jail disguised as a washerwoman, a woman who does laundry.

clue.text: Go mad before long — it's not serious

parts.note: to flip is to lose one's temper or go crazy
to long for something is to pant for it

explanation.surface: Someone warns that going mad before long is no laughing matter, or perhaps that it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Flippant describes a light, disrespectful attitude that treats grave things as trivial.

clue.text: Old Dracula's characteristic feature

definitions.meaning: an idiom for elderly, from horses whose gums recede with age
the vampire is known for his elongated fangs

explanation.surface: An ageing Dracula's most famous trait.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for elderly comes from judging a horse's age by its teeth; read literally, it describes a vampire's fangs.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means elderly, and literally describes the vampire's lengthy fangs.

clue.text: Petition in newspapers

definitions.meaning: to petition someone is to urge or ... them for something
the collective name for newspapers and journalists

explanation.surface: A petition is printed in the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means urge or plead with; as a noun it means the newspaper industry.

clue.text: Ham and a well-ripened cheese finally sent up

indicators.note: in a down entry, sending up the last letter means moving it higher, earlier in the word

parts.note: a cheese that is well ripened is described as mature

explanation.surface: A deli order: ham, and a mature cheese delivered to the upstairs room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' looks like a cold meat but means a poor performer. MATURE has its final E moved up two places to make MATEUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham is an unskilled, over-the-top actor; ham radio operators are likewise non-professional hobbyists.

clue.text: Make inroads into attempt for agreement

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the word for an attempt

parts.note: a try is an attempt
to eat into something is to make inroads into it

explanation.surface: Negotiators try to make progress towards a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between nations, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Operation could make Clement happier

indicators.note: could make says the letters of the following words can be rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: A surgery that might leave an elderly patient called Clement feeling better.
explanation.definitionFit: Replacing a worn hip joint with a prosthesis is a common surgical operation.

clue.text: Exit on cue for moving performance

indicators.note: moving says the letters of the stage direction are shifted about

explanation.surface: An actor leaves the stage exactly on cue in an emotional show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' seems to praise the performance but signals the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The execution of a task or piece of music is the way it is carried out or performed.

clue.text: Eliminate answer in Gaelic language

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for answer inside the name of the language

parts.note: Erse is an old name for Scottish or Irish Gaelic

explanation.surface: Getting rid of a solution written in Gaelic.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to wipe out or remove completely, a synonym for eliminate.

clue.text: Maybe fifth set of French drink

parts.note: de is French for 'of'
cider is an alcoholic drink made from apples

explanation.surface: Perhaps a fifth set of drinks ordered at a French bar.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis a fifth set settles a match level at two sets each.
explanation.definitionFit: A final set that settles a tied match is called the decider; 'maybe' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Examine bug picking up tip from phone

indicators.note: picking up says the creature takes something into itself

parts.note: a bug is an insect

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone examines a phone for a listening device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' suggests a covert microphone, but it is a creepy-crawly here.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to look over carefully, a direct synonym for examine.

clue.text: French composer mocking work rejecting king

indicators.note: rejecting says the abbreviation for king is thrown out of the mocking piece

parts.note: a satire is a work that mocks its target
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A French composer writes a satirical piece that snubs the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Erik Satie was a French composer, known for the Gymnopédies.

clue.text: Drops the crocks? See what results

definitions.text: Drops the crocks? See what results

indicators.note: to crock is to break or damage, so the two words before it are broken up

explanation.surface: Someone clumsy drops the crockery; just look at the outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crocks' reads as a noun for pots but works as a verb meaning breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A potsherd is a broken fragment of pottery, exactly what dropped crockery leaves behind.

clue.text: Article on back mostly in horse ride?

definitions.text: Article on back mostly in horse ride?

indicators.note: in places the article and the shortened back within the ride

parts.note: a hack is a ride on horseback

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece on another means it sits above it

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: mostly says the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: verso is the back of a page

explanation.surface: A bag carried on the back, perhaps on a horse ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A haversack is a bag slung over the back, an item one might take hacking on horseback.

clue.text: Heartless Britney Spears upset someone en route

indicators.note: upset says the letters of the singer's surname are knocked over and rearranged
heartless means the middle of the first name is removed, keeping its ends

explanation.surface: The pop star Britney Spears, cold-hearted and upset, encounters someone on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A passer-by is a person who happens to be going past, someone on their way somewhere.

clue.text: Disciple left out for a time, I gave up religion

indicators.note: out for says one letter leaves and another piece takes its place

parts.note: an apostle is a disciple of Jesus

explanation.surface: A follower who stepped away for a while confesses to abandoning their faith.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate is one who renounces a faith; the clue lets the renegade speak in the first person.

clue.text: Top-class seaside venue featuring old rock band

indicators.note: featuring says the seaside structure has the band inside it

parts.note: a pier often hosts shows at British seaside resorts
REM was an American rock band, disbanded in 2011

explanation.surface: A top seaside concert venue has a veteran rock group on the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Premier means foremost or of the highest rank, like a premier league.

clue.text: Dave almost OK getting drunk — with this?

definitions.text: Dave almost OK getting drunk — with this?

indicators.note: getting drunk says the letters are made unsteady and rearranged
almost says the name loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: Dave is nearly fine, but getting tipsy; maybe on this spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: DAV, Dave without its last letter, joins OK, and the five letters are mixed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Vodka is a spirit that could well be the cause of someone's drunkenness.

clue.text: DOS kept crashing computer

indicators.note: crashing suggests a computer failure, but signals the letters are smashed and reordered

explanation.surface: An old operating system kept failing on a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: DOS is the old Microsoft operating system.
explanation.definitionFit: A desktop is a personal computer designed to sit on a desk.

clue.text: Someone in routine job can up and drink

parts.note: a cog in a machine is someone doing a small routine part

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A worker in a dull job opens a can and has a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a French brandy, a type of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Manage part of poem in Old English

indicators.note: in says the poem section sits inside the abbreviation

parts.note: a verse is a stanza, part of a poem

explanation.surface: Someone copes with a section of an Anglo-Saxon poem.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise or direct, the same as manage.

clue.text: Kid influenced by speech

indicators.note: by speech says the word is to be heard, not read

parts.note: to be swayed is to be influenced

explanation.surface: A child persuaded by an address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child but means the young goat's soft leather.
explanation.definitionFit: Kid is leather from young goats, often finished with a napped surface like this material.

clue.text: Gold goes up in price then flags

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold
a price that goes up rises

explanation.surface: Gold rises in value, then sags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flags' looks like a verb meaning weakens, but is the plural of a plant name: flag is a kind of iris.
explanation.definitionFit: Orris is a type of iris, and flag is another name for the iris plant.

clue.text: Simple part of church I should enter

indicators.note: should enter says the letter goes inside the church part

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church

explanation.surface: An uncomplicated area of a church that I ought to go into.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means innocent or unsophisticated, so simple in the sense of artless.

clue.text: Maybe fan of bit-part player and thespian sharing a part

parts.note: an extra is a film actor in a minor non-speaking role

indicators.note: sharing a part says one letter A serves both words, so the second loses it

parts.note: a thespian is an actor

explanation.surface: An admirer of a minor film actor and a stage actor who share a role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fan' looks like an admirer but is an air-moving device; 'maybe' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An extractor fan removes stale air, so a fan is one example of an extractor.

clue.text: Old campaigner, note, following my naval vessel

indicators.note: following says the veteran and the note come after the exclamation

parts.note: cor is an exclamation like 'my!'
a vet is a veteran, an old campaigner
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A veteran sailor writes a note on a warship.
explanation.definitionFit: A corvette is a small, lightly armed warship used for escort duties.

clue.text: Agent welcomes rest for bounder on TV once

indicators.note: welcomes says the agent takes the rest inside

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
kip is British slang for sleep or a rest

explanation.surface: A secret agent welcomes a break from a cad on old television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bounder' suggests a cad but means a jumper: Skippy the Bush Kangaroo was a 1960s Australian TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: The title kangaroo of a 1960s Australian children's series bounded about the bush.
